text:
ana: Quick iteration posted for notification preview in SLO alerting. Screenshot attached: https://img.redwood.test/ui/preview-v2.png. Qs: 1) Layout: compact chips row vs vertical stack? 2) Suppression wording: full reason vs condensed? 3) How to indicate fallback routing (icon vs text)? :sparkles:

sam: For narrow panels, chips will overflow awkwardly. I prefer chips for <=2 channels, stack for 3+. Could auto-wrap but keyboard navigation needs to remain linear.

priya: Accessibility notes: chips must have clear focus outlines and unique aria-labels (`aria-label="channel: email"`). Color: current suppression yellow fails AA; consider `#f7c948` -> `#f5b21b` or add a darker border. Also ensure suppressed state is announced by screen readers when the preview changes.

matt: Copy idea: condensed `Suppressed · schedule` as default with full text on hover. Also consider `Muted until 12:00` vs `Suppressed until 12:00` (tone). I think `Muted` reads friendlier but `Suppressed` is more precise.

jordan: Routing visual: if we show priority order, stacked makes sense. For fallback, a small chevron+label `fallback: regional` seems more explicit than an icon-only affordance. Could hide the label behind expansion on compact screens.

ana: ana: Plan: responsive layout (chips -> stack), condensed suppression copy with tooltip, label the fallback in-line for clarity. @sam please propose aria patterns and keyboard flow.

sam: Will prototype. Suggest `role=region` with `aria-labelledby` pointing to preview header, and `aria-live="polite"` for suppression updates. Badges should be `role=status` and focusable.

design-bot: Figma updated: https://www.figma.com/file/yyy notification-preview/stack-vs-chips

ana: Action items: @priya to update a11y checklist, @matt to produce 3 microcopy options (formal/neutral/friendly), @sam to demo keyboard interaction, @jordan to verify layout with sample routing data. Sync Friday 11am.

priya: I'll include contrast numbers and suggested CSS tokens.
